Dormant on the console path but real for any embedding host passing `data` as a prop (rows arriving after mount are never shown), and the fix shape is specified: destructure `data: dataProp` and depend on that one value (⛔ not `rest` — refetch-every-render trap the body names); seed the clustering zoom from the applied initial camera or first `onZoom`. Both items one PR in `packages/plugin-map/src/ObjectMap.tsx`, with tests for the prop-update path. **Serial constraint**: #5020 edits the same file (doc comment) — claim whichever lands first and merge main before the second; note the overlap in the claim comment. Size/model suggestion: S–M, sonnet.

Clause-②: **no** — neither item changes what the contract accepts or rejects, and nothing on the public surface widens. Item 1 makes an existing declared prop actually tracked after mount; item 2 corrects an internal seed. No schema key gains or loses acceptance.
Serial constraints cleared: **#5020** is the one card triage named as editing this same file (its `clusterRadius` doc comment) — it is `pm:queue`, **unassigned, not in flight**, so there is no live hold and this claim takes the file first. Open PRs hold disjoint surfaces, each measured by `git diff --name-only origin/main...`: PR #5290 → `apps/console/**`; PR #5292 → `eslint-rules/**` + `eslint.config.js`; PR #5294 → `packages/plugin-view/**`. No in-flight card is known to touch `packages/plugin-map`; if one turns out to, stop and report.

## Scope — both items, one PR, `Fixes #5003`

Triage promoted this `finding` → `pm:queue` · Task on 2026-08-19 and specified the fix shape. Carried through:

**Item 1 — `props.data` is read by the fetch effect but is not one of its dependencies.** ⛔ Do **not** add `rest` to the deps array: `rest` is a fresh object every render, so naming it converts the bug into a refetch-every-render trap. The narrow fix the card names is to destructure the prop (`data: dataProp`) and depend on **that one value**. The eslint `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` warnings already reported on this effect (for `rest` and `schema`) are the signal, not the specification — satisfying the linter is not the goal, threading the prop correctly is.

**Item 2 — the clustering zoom seed never sees the initial camera.** `useState(mapConfig.zoom || 3)` seeds what `clusterMarkers` uses for grid cell size, and `onZoom` is the only writer. MapLibre's constructor applies the initial camera via `initialViewState` *before* react-map-gl attaches React handlers, so no `onZoom` ever fires for it. Seed from the applied initial camera (or the first `onZoom`).

## Verification the report must carry

The card documents **why this is dormant**, and that is exactly what makes it easy to "fix" without evidence:

- the console path never passes `data` as a prop (it goes through `ElementDataSourceGate` and the component's own `dataSource.find`);
- every fetch sets `loading` back to `true`, which unmounts and remounts `MapGL`, so a data change *through the effect* is always reflected;
- clustering only engages above 100 markers (or explicit opt-in).

So a test that renders through the console path will pass before **and** after — it proves nothing. **Test the prop-update path directly**: mount with `data={[]}`, then pass rows, and assert the rows are shown. Reverse-verify: predict which assertions go red with the fix reverted, name them before running, and report predicted-vs-observed. If an assertion is green on both legs, it is not pinning the fix — say so rather than counting it.

Item 2's own note: this was equally true before #4941 (the seed was then the synthesized `10`); that PR did not introduce it and the current `3` is closer to a fitted continental camera than `10` was. Recorded so it is not re-reported as a regression of #4941.
